title: SANS & Cephalad Fluid Shift Review
trigger_patterns: Near vision acuity shift or optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD) exceeds individual baseline band
Crew reports progressive visual blur, difficulty reading small checklists, or orbital fullness
Routine mission surveillance protocol for long-duration microgravity exposure

steps.text: Perform standard near-vision acuity assessment with the onboard Jaeger/tumbling-E reading card under calibrated 500 lux cabin lighting.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: Record refractive change delta in diopters and compare against the pre-flight baseline in the crew tablet.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: Deploy the ocular ultrasound probe to measure bilateral Optic Nerve Sheath Diameter (ONSD) 3.0 mm posterior to the globe.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: Check for secondary SANS signs: optic disc margin elevation, cotton wool spots, choroidal folds, or globe posterior flattening.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: Schedule prescribed Lower Body Negative Pressure (LBNP / Chibis) session (25-35 mmHg caudal suction for 60 min) to pull fluid away from the head.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: Adjust crew tablet and console UI display ergonomics: increase font scaling by +20%, set high-contrast dark mode, and verify helmet visor focal clearance.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: Queue encrypted ocular ultrasound cine loops and subjective symptom log for ground flight surgeon review over the next mission pass.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure
